title: HI96800 Refractometer for Refractive Index and Brix Measurements
locator: Specifications, p. 6. Calibration, measurement and scale selection, pp. 11–13. Sucrose check solution, p. 15.
summary: The HI96800 can display the measured refractive index, an index compensated to 20 °C, or °Brix. The guide explains how to zero with water, cover the prism and check the Brix scale with a sucrose solution.
scope: The compensated index scale ends at 1.5040. Choose the scale required by the experiment and check that the expected sample falls within range.
rights: Manufacturer manual linked from the Hanna Instruments HI96800 product page. Original summary.

title: Guidelines on Objective Tests to Determine Quality of Fruits and Vegetables and Dry and Dried Produce
publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
locator: Taking the samples, p. 3. Refractometer test for total soluble solids, pp. 4–8, including the zero check, sample preparation and reporting.
summary: The OECD describes how to obtain a representative fruit juice sample, check the instrument using water and a sucrose solution, and report soluble solids in °Brix. It gives fruit-specific guidance for obtaining juice.
scope: Most useful for ripe, juicy fruit. Record the part of the fruit sampled and the temperature correction used. Other dissolved substances can contribute to the Brix reading.

title: Biochemical, nutritional, and nutraceutical properties of cactus pear accessions
version: Tunç et al., volume 15, article 19755. DOI 10.1038/s41598-025-04726-6
locator: Materials and methods, subsection on total soluble solids, pH, titratable acidity and moisture. Table 2 and the accompanying discussion of accessions CP81 and CP53.
summary: The researchers measured clarified cactus pear juice with a Hanna HI96800. Across 100 accessions, total soluble solids ranged from 9.01 to 16.63 °Brix. The paper reports reducing sugars separately.
scope: The range describes the accessions sampled in Türkiye. Use the same juice preparation when comparing fruit lots and measure individual sugars separately if their identity matters.
rights: Original summary and link to the authors’ open-access paper.

title: ACCC objective measures: measuring Brix or Baumé in grape juice and must
publisher: Australian Wine Research Institute and Wine Australia
version: Wilkes and Hirlam, final report AWR 1701-3.3.4, September 2022
locator: Grape juice guideline, pp. 37–40. See the juice extraction figure, the digital refractometer workflow and Validation Requirements.
summary: The guideline describes sampling a grape lot, extracting and clarifying its juice, checking the refractometer at zero and recording a temperature-aware reading. It calls for an independent comparison before the facility adopts the method.
scope: Written for grape juice and must at receival. The HI96800 provides °Brix. Other instruments may also offer the Baumé scale discussed in the report.
rights: Publisher-hosted final report and original summary.

title: Assessment of Variability Sources in Grape Ripening Parameters by Using FTIR and Multivariate Modelling
version: Schorn-García et al., volume 12, article 962. DOI 10.3390/foods12050962
locator: Sections 2.2–2.3, berry sampling and Brix reference measurements. Section 3.5 and Table 5, sources of variability in the reference results.
summary: The investigators measured individual grape berries with a Hanna HI96801 to compare soluble solids across harvest dates and positions on the vine. Their joint analysis of Brix and pH found that maturity and position on the plant influenced the reference measurements.
scope: The study used the HI96801 and measured individual berries. A pooled grape juice result answers a different sampling question. FTIR predictions in the article use a separate instrument and model.
rights: Original summary and link to the authors’ open-access paper.

title: Harmonised Methods of the International Honey Commission: determination of moisture
locator: Water determination, pp. 9–12, especially the 20 °C conversion table. The separate digital-instrument comparison begins on p. 13.
summary: The method relates a honey sample’s refractive index at 20 °C to grams of water per 100 grams of honey. It includes duplicate readings and a conversion table covering 13–25 g/100 g.
scope: The formal procedure and precision estimates apply to an Abbé refractometer. An accompanying comparison evaluated three digital models. Transferring the method to an HI96800 requires checking its index range and agreement on representative honeys.

title: Honiganalyse: Bestimmung des Wassergehalts in Honig
version: German-language Honiganalyse brochure, publisher file Honiganalyse2023.pdf
locator: Pages 2–3, especially the Chataway conversion table and HI96800 section on p. 3.
summary: Hanna illustrates how to use the HI96800 refractive-index reading with a honey moisture table at 20 °C. Page 2 separately discusses the correction needed when using the sucrose scale.
scope: Manufacturer guidance for honey. A raw Brix value measures equivalent sucrose concentration. Choose the honey table appropriate to the scale and stay within the meter’s stated range.
rights: Manufacturer-hosted German-language application guidance and original English summary.

title: Honey type diversity in a Ligurian honeybee sanctuary: Australia’s Kangaroo Island honey across a decadal fire-impacted landscape
version: Barbour et al., volume 160, article 293. DOI 10.1007/s44473-026-00307-1
locator: Materials and methods, physicochemical analysis paragraph naming the HI96800. Results, Physicochemical characterisation of honey groups, Table 5.
summary: The authors used a Hanna HI96800 and converted refractive index at 20 °C to honey moisture with a published chart. In representative blends from three honey groups, moisture ranged from 16.4% to 18.4%.
scope: These are measurements of Kangaroo Island blends. The study gives an example of reporting results on this model. Local precision, the sample’s state and the table selection still affect an individual determination.
rights: Original summary and link to the publisher’s research article.
